title: 2026 第三届动漫游戏节正式上线，全球二次元佳作集结盛夏
text:
经过前两届的持续积累与社区沉淀，2026第三届动漫游戏节于今日在 Steam 平台正式上线，活动将持续至 9 月 14 日。本届以”沉浸式动漫游戏体验”为年度主张，将全球范围内的动漫风格佳作、独立新锐力量与广大爱好者汇聚在同一片数字空间之中，从今天起，探索、体验与分享同步开启。
【活动 详情 】
活动时间：2026 年 9 月 8 日至 9 月 14 日
参与游戏：超过600款精选动漫风格游戏
活动页面：https://store.steampowered.com/curator/46138335/sale/AnimeGameFestival2026
官方网站：https://www.nlentmt.com/anime-game-festival-2026-cn
【本届亮点】
精品矩阵集中亮相 ： 本届活动汇聚了来自全球开发者的动漫风格游戏，覆盖角色扮演、动作冒险、策略模拟、休闲治愈等多个品类。无论是深耕二次元领域多年的成熟作品，还是首次公开亮相的独立新作，均经过筛选后集中呈现，让不同偏好的玩家都能在这一周内找到心仪之选。
限定优惠同步开放 ： 活动期间，多款参展作品将推出限时特卖与专属折扣。对于此前观望已久的玩家而言，这是入手经典作品的理想窗口；对于希望拓展游戏库的新观众而言，也是以更友好价格尝试新类型的契机。
试玩先行体验前置 ： 部分参展作品将在活动期间提供 Demo 试玩版本，覆盖不同体量、不同类型，玩家可在购买前先行体验核心玩法与美术风格。
为新锐开发者搭台 ： 本届活动继续保留对独立团队与新锐创作者的重点推荐位。在人气大作之外，一批具有独特视角与实验性玩法的作品将获得集中曝光，帮助玩家发现那些尚未被广泛关注但品质出色的作品。
【参展阵容】
限时特卖阵容中将有多款人气作品已确认参与，覆盖【剧情冒险】、【肉鸽动作】、【卡牌策略】、【多人合作】等品类，玩家可在活动期间以限定折扣入手。
在试玩首发阵容中，《公会创世纪》《守城英雄传》《远征公会》《少女机师养成计划：女武神协议》《怪奇餐厅》等游戏将带来 Demo 试玩版本或Playtest 测试活动，涵盖【模拟养成】、【经营建造】、【塔防策略】等方向，让玩家在购买前先行体验核心内容。
此外，由独立开发团队打造的《审判官谢泼德》《地狱不空》《勇者小队全灭了。》《睡前派对》等创意新锐游戏亮相，在这个盛夏让每一位参与者都能找到属于自己的“次元之选”。更多参展作品信息已在Steam 活动页面更新，玩家可持续关注。
【往届回顾】
动漫游戏节自创办以来始终保持与玩家和厂商的紧密连接。首届与第二届活动均获得了玩家群体与游戏厂商的积极反馈，两届累计汇聚数百款动漫风格作品，覆盖数百万次社区曝光与互动。第三届在延续核心定位的基础上，进一步优化了参展结构、丰富了推荐维度，力求为所有参与者提供更完整的体验。
【关于动漫游戏节】
动漫游戏节由 Neverland Entertainment 主办，致力于为全球动漫风格游戏开发者与玩家搭建一个高效连接、互相发现的平台。每一届活动都围绕”让好游戏被看见、让同好者相遇”这一核心目标展开，覆盖从成熟大作到独立新锐的全谱系作品。第三届动漫游戏节已于今日正式上线，活动将持续至 9 月 14 日。

title: 全员带包刚枪爽，CF船新版本重生爆破来袭
text:
9月8日， 穿越火线 「无限爆破」版本正式上线。本次版本的核心是全新重生爆破模式，在经典爆破的基础上引入三包点、重生复活与积分制三项核心改动。除此之外，版本还带来了投掷训练扩容、排位体验优化、个性化自定义系统上线，以及成长型加特林三相真灵、绒绒虎玩偶装饰等一批新内容。无论是喜欢对枪战斗爽的团竞玩家、热衷钻研包点战术的爆破老兵，还是只想上线领一份免费礼包的休闲CFer，这个九月都是惊喜满满。
重生爆破：三包点无限复活，爆破模式迎来玩法重构
重生爆破是本次版本最值得关注的内容，堪称穿越火线在爆破玩法方向上动作最大的一次改动。
模式基于经典爆破制作，角色HP、防具、武器性能、移动与战斗判定等底层规则完全沿用现有爆破设定，老兵进局几乎没有上手门槛。核心改动集中在三点，攻防双方均可在被击败后快速重新加入战局、包点数量从2个增加至3个、胜负判定从回合胜场改为爆破分数累计。
规则改动看似简洁，实际带来的对局节奏变化相当显著。
复活机制是整个模式的底层逻辑所在。传统爆破中，死亡意味着该回合退出战斗，容错空间极低。然而在重生爆破中，双方默认复活时间为5秒，死亡后即可快速重新加入战局，场上人数始终保持动态平衡。潜伏方全员持有C4，安装不消耗、死亡不掉落、复活后自动补发，甚至可在多个包点同时下包。保卫方不再是”拆掉包即可获胜”，而是在整个回合周期内持续压制潜伏方的得分进度，攻防双方的对抗节奏更接近持续拉扯，而非单点决胜。对那些想玩到更轻度的爆破老兵来说，这套复活机制带来的对枪连续感是实实在在的体验改善。
不仅如此，三包点的设计更进一步拓展了战术选择空间。每局开局，三个包点将随机分配3分、2分、1分三档分值，分值在对应包点被引爆时结算给潜伏方。引爆单个包点不结束回合，仅当所有包点全部引爆时回合才会提前结束，已引爆的包点随即移除，不可再次安装C4。这套得分机制促使潜伏方在每一局中都需要做出明确的战术选择，是集中资源强攻高分包点快速建立优势，还是分兵多点同时施压、让保卫方疲于应对，不同的打法路线会在三包点的拉扯中体现出明显的策略分野。
地图配置方面，重生爆破目前提供异域小镇-竞技荣耀、港口-竞技荣耀、供电所-竞技荣耀三张地图，每局随机选取两张，每张地图进行两个回合，回合结束后双方阵营互换。最终爆破总分更高的一方获胜，双方分数相同则判定为平局，平局双方均不获得胜利奖励，可谓是每分必争。
整体来看，重生爆破在降低容错门槛的同时，并没有因此弱化策略层面的深度。无限复活带来了更流畅的对枪体验，三包点带来了更丰富的战术决策空间，两者的结合让这个模式在对枪爽感和战术博弈之间找到了一个相对的平衡点。
竞技与系统优化：投掷练图扩容，举报也加贡献等级
玩法之外，本次版本在竞技体验和系统层面也更新了一批针对性优化。
竞技方向，投掷训练模式迎来扩容，新黑色城镇、新沙漠灰、新鹰眼-CFPL十周年纪念版、新姑苏城、供电所-竞技荣耀五张地图新增官方投掷点位教学引导，将此前CFer需要自行研究或依赖外部攻略的投掷点位知识直接内置进游戏，为长期在练习图反复摸索投掷落点的钻研型老兵省去了不少功夫。
为了利于投掷道具的使用，供电所-竞技荣耀新增了掩体结构调整，移除了潜伏者中路上侧部分掩体和B通出口上侧掩体，并降低了中路左侧上侧掩体的建筑高度。掩体高度和覆盖范围的收窄，直接降低了投掷物被遮挡的可能，烟雾、闪光的落点选择会将更加灵活，整体战术选择的丰富度也随之提升。
排位体验方面，枪王排位新增败局守护增益。与以往排位不掉分保护卡类道具不同，这个增益不随赛季重置，获取后在没有使用前持续保留，对长期活跃在排位的竞技老兵来说更为实用。
系统层面也有小改动。个性化自定义系统正式上线，名片、喷漆、击杀图标等个性化配置集中至统一入口管理，在个人仓库点击个性化装扮即可进入，包含加载画面资料卡、名片资料卡、交互、游玩、音效五大类别，解决了相关设置分散在不同入口的体验问题。
举报分系统也同样迎来更新。新增的举报贡献等级根据玩家举报成功率、举报次数、被举报人处罚等维度综合评估，为长期认真参与举报的CFer建立了明确的正向反馈机制。贡献等级达到S级后可解锁追加处罚权益，SS级进一步开放加速审核，每日可申请1次、最快1天内收到结果，SSS级则享有高优处理特权，提交举报后官方将优先受理并对该场对局发起重点检测。贡献等级越高，手里的举报权重越实在。
新道具与版本福利：三相真灵三形态切换，登录即可领取鎏金水墨
全新成长型加特林三相真灵是这次版本主打的新武器。这把武器的核心机制在于形态切换系统，每回合随机刷新形态，熔晶与冰狱两种形态支持手动切换，另有小概率触发邪王形态。三种形态各有对应的强化属性，熔晶形态对命中敌人造成额外伤害，冰狱形态附带减速与流血效果，邪王形态同时兼备前两种效果。升级路线从Lv1到Lv7满级共需消耗1000进化水晶，满级后可继续抽取万化装扮，三种玩偶全部收集后自动获得三相主宰者玩偶，装备该玩偶可提升邪王形态的触发概率，为满级老兵提供了额外的养成目标。
交易兑换所上线了全新的绒绒虎玩偶装饰宝箱，消耗3个高级令牌可兑换一个，开箱随机获得两款隐藏玩偶装饰或六款普通玩偶装饰之一，装备至对应白虎系列武器上会触发专属动画效果。王者夺宝、王者轮回、王者许愿三个奖池本期都进行了奖励刷新，喜欢抽奖的CFer可以进入游戏一探究竟。
福利方面，9月8日版本更新完毕后登录游戏即可领取版本礼包，内含新USP-鎏金水墨、骰子1个及666火线币，领取窗口持续至10月19日，门槛超低上线就能到手。爆破补给库一并上线，在重生爆破模式中完成任务积累积分，可兑换暗月套装等奖励。掌火平台配套新增重生日设活动，感兴趣的CFer可前往生成专属人设卡片。
总而言之，老兵们最关心的当然还是新模式好不好玩，重生爆破在玩法定位上填补了兼顾刚枪爽感与战术深度、同时降低回合容错压力这一此前相对空缺的体验区间，最终能否真正在老兵群体中打开局面，还是要等实战来检验。9月8日新版本上线先把礼包领好，叫上队友开一局重生爆破，三包点周旋见真章。随后9月20日更有至尊王者系列升级接档，手里攒着王者枪械的老玩家，可以提前期待一下。

title: 突破品效合一瓶颈！LoopMe 升级 PurchaseLoop，以 AI 赋能 CPI 与 CPA 深度转化
text:
近日，全球领先的广告科技平台 LoopMe 正式宣布升级旗下品牌效果广告投放平台 PurchaseLoop，推出全新的 下端漏斗效果解决方案 （Lower-funnel Performance） ，聚焦于单次下载成本（CPI）与单次转化成本（CPA）的能力优化，由此打破品牌与效果壁垒，赋能全链路下端漏斗转化。
当前，苹果 ATT 隐私新规的落地导致信号缺失，传统渠道获客成本随之持续攀升，用户也在加速从网页端向 App 端转移。如何将中上端积累的品牌声量，有效转化为可衡量的下端漏斗效果正成为营销人员面临的挑战。
LoopMe 全新推出的 Lower-funnel Performance 解决方案能够帮助广告主借助品牌曝光过程中积累的受众画像与兴趣意向信号，有效推动下漏斗效果广告转化。该解决方案可覆盖两大转化场景： Performance App  专注于移动应用下载及安装后行为转化，如首单购买、首次订阅及应用内 ROAS 提升； Performance Web  则专注于网页端的客户获取、线索收集、注册转化及网站 ROAS 优化。两大场景均采用千次展示成本（CPM）结算模式。现阶段将先从已合作过 PurchaseLoop 的客户开始测试, 赋能品牌将前期积累的受众洞察真正转化为驱动底层转化的实际效能。
Lower-funnel Performance 充分依托 LoopMe 现有的消费者数据与技术生态，实现了从品牌曝光到效果转化的无缝衔接。在品牌曝光与触达阶段，平台通过 AI 驱动的全域基础受众建模，帮助广告主构建精准的用户画像；在品牌互动阶段，借助兴趣互动广告精准捕捉用户的意图信号，筛选出高价值受众；在购买意图阶段，结合 Chartboost SDK 覆盖的全球 5 万多个应用内行为数据，将多元信号实时注入 2400 多个 AI 模型中进行动态训练与预测，精准锁定具有转化潜力的目标人群；最终在 CPI 与 CPA 优化阶段，完成深度转化目标的落地。
这一 AI 驱动的全链路转化能力已在实战投放中得到充分验证。以欧洲领先的在线宠物零售商 Zooplus 为例，该品牌此前在六个欧洲核心市场推广猫粮时面临销售增长的挑战。LoopMe 通过 AI 优化、预测建模和定制受众定向的组合策略，帮助 Zooplus 实现了规模化的高效拓客，不仅取得了强劲的转化率，表现也优于公开交易市场。最终，Zooplus 在六个市场的整体广告支出回报率（ROAS）达到 $1.71，其中法国市场更是创下了 $4.42 的亮眼成绩，充分展现出该技术在规模化驱动销售增长方面的卓越成效。
在实际应用与效果衡量层面，广告主无需调整现有采买模式或更换数据监测体系，即可无缝启用下端漏斗转化模型，投放效果直接通过现有的移动测量伙伴（MMP）或转化追踪工具即可完成评估。
LoopMe 代理商合作伙伴关系副总裁 Andy Sophocli 表示：“ PurchaseLoop 旨在帮助广告主充分挖掘并释放受众数据的商业价值。通过将用户行为数据与下端漏斗转化结果无缝链接，PurchaseLoop 能更精准地支持 CPI 与 CPA 优化，助力广告主在同一平台内实现品牌宣传与效果广告的高效共管。 ”
关于 LoopMe：
LoopMe 是全球领先的品牌效果广告平台。公司首创将人工智能引入品牌广告及智能广告交易市场，以消费者洞察与 AI 为核心，助力品牌和合作平台通过 Chartboost SDK 直连高质量移动流量、网页端与CTV流量，实现更优绩效表现。LoopMe 成立于 2012 年，总部位于英国，在全球设有办事处，包括纽约、波士顿、亚特兰大、芝加哥、底特律、旧金山、洛杉矶、多伦多、新加坡、悉尼、墨尔本、第聂伯罗、克拉科夫、北京、上海和香港。更多信息请访问：https://loopme.cn/。

title: He went to Africa to work as a mercenary
text:
On the morning of the sixth day of the Lunar New Year, Brother Zhong, who runs the Paodao Studio in Madagascar, was still asleep when a phone call from his translator roused him from bed.
“They’re causing a commotion,” the interpreter said over the phone. “They’re on strike.”
The workers who had been on duty the night before stopped working, and those who were supposed to be on the early shift that morning also stayed indoors and refused to work. There were about fifty or sixty of them—the entire workforce from both shifts—and they practically packed the studio to capacity. They had coordinated their actions and launched their protest in unison.
When Brother Zhong arrived, he was the only Chinese person in the room. The workers were sitting down, so Brother Zhong told them to stand up. “I’m your boss. I’m much older than you—probably even older than your fathers—so it’s rude of you to sit there like that.”
Once the workers got up, Brother Zhong went over everything with them point by point: he explained that their wages were already higher than the market rate; since the night shift ran from 7:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. the next morning—which was too long—he had taken the initiative to provide each of them with eggs and baguettes as a late-night snack;Tea, sugar, and meal allowances—he paid for all of them out of his own pocket. “None of this was part of our agreement; I added these for you on my own.”
But this did not sway the workers; they stood firm on one point: they demanded a 20 percent wage increase, or they would all walk out together—“Malaysians must help Malaysians.”
Zhong Ge was at a loss and could only say that, under these circumstances, he couldn’t continue working. He then told the workers through an interpreter that anyone who wanted to leave could take their pay and go.
“In the end, half of them left, and half stayed.” Brother Zhong recalled later that he was facing the pressure of a sudden surge in orders at the time, and the workers had clearly counted on this to go on strike. “The translator remarked with some emotion that they had planned it all out—they were determined to walk out together no matter what—but they didn’t expect that, since you’d generally treated them well, half of them ended up staying.”
A dinner gathering for the workers at Zhong Ge Studio
Just a few days before this strike, Brother Zhong had sent red envelopes to everyone, and a photo of their lively dinner together was still posted on his profile page. “Half the people in that picture had already left.”
After the strike, Brother Zhong came to this conclusion: “You can’t be too nice to them. They haven’t been through the trials of a market economy or the industrial age; if you’re nice to them, they’ll think you can’t do without them.We’ve gone through decades of reform and opening up, so we understand that when others treat us well, it means they respect us. But they think that if you’re nice to me, it’s because you can’t do without me—so I can shamelessly demand higher wages and better benefits from you.”
01
A Land Blessed by Heaven
That strike, which had driven away half the workforce, became a topic that Brother Zhong and his employees avoided discussing. He simply gave a pay raise to the half of the workers who had chosen to stay at the time. “The employees who left considered them traitors, but they knew full well that staying was the right decision.”
From an economic standpoint, turning down this job is certainly not a wise choice for young people in the area.
The unemployment rate in Madagascar ranges from 70 to 80 percent—a figure Brother Zhong observed after running a business there for two years. The country’s per capita monthly income is equivalent to only 300 to 350 yuan. In his view, “This is a country that has failed in governance; it’s very, very bad.”
But there is no direct correlation between poverty and happiness. Zhong Ge found that although young people in Madagascar don’t have much money, they are no less happy for it. “Young people in Africa are happy; their sense of well-being is not necessarily any less than ours.”
This joy has its roots in nature. Madagascar is a tropical island with no winter, so there’s no risk of freezing to death, and food is easy to come by. As Brother Zhong puts it, “You can lie under a coconut tree, wait for a ripe coconut to fall, take a few sips, and you’ll survive.” If you’re really short on protein,“just go catch some fish—all it takes is a little fishing.” The cost of survival is extremely low; this is a blessing from heaven bestowed upon this land, and it also provides the natural conditions for the locals’ “laid-back” lifestyle.
Brother Zhong noticed that people here only bought enough rice for a single meal—“one jin of rice, half a jin of rice”—and no one ever bought a whole bag of rice to take home. Except for the top one percent of extremely wealthy families, ordinary people generally had no surplus grain; they always had just enough to get by for the day.
This way of life has also shaped a unique lifestyle. Young people love to play soccer, and the sport is extremely popular; the country has even finished as runner-up in the Africa Cup of Nations. Brother Zhong still remembers how people celebrated when the team made it to the final: “They grabbed basins and steel pots and banged on them until the whole city was making noise.”
On Friday nights, small groups of people would drive up in cars or on motorcycles, grab a bottle of beer, and sit by the roadside chatting. Brother Zhong once asked the translator curiously, “With all the chaos in this country, wouldn’t that lead to fights?” He replied, “No, no—everyone’s just happy and having a good time at this hour.”
Sunday is a day off that locals never miss, no matter what. This is also the time that gives Brother Zhong the most headaches: “They take Sundays very seriously; they have to go to church.”Not only do his workers take the day off, but on this day, the entire capital comes to a standstill. On the capital’s busiest street—the equivalent of Beijing’s Wangfujing—‘all the shops and restaurants are closed.’ Locals gather in groups of three or five to have picnics, socialize, and enjoy their day off.”
“They’re living a slow life,” Brother Zhong said. “We can’t say it’s wrong—it’s just a different way of life.” In his view, if we were to have a deep discussion about happiness, he said, “You really wouldn’t know who’s happier.”
However, this lifestyle poses a hurdle for any Chinese person looking to start a business here. The most obvious example of this is that as soon as they get paid at the end of the month, they disappear.
Zhong Ge specifically asked them why they did this, and the answer he received was hard for him to swallow. “His logic went like this: ‘I’m broke, so I need a job. The whole point of working is to make money. So if I’ve worked my butt off for a whole month and earned all that money, why would I still need to work? Am I crazy or something?’”
Because of this difference in perspective, the size of Zhong Ge’s studio has never lived up to his expectations. “We had 50 people during the Spring Festival, and we’re still at 50 today. I’ve always wanted to grow it to over 100 people, but I just can’t seem to get there.”
The workers at Zhong Ge’s Studio
The same dilemma is evident in “Brother Bao”’s studio. This Zhejiang-born entrepreneur, who didn’t even graduate from high school, spent many years making his way in eight African countries before settling in Madagascar in 2022, where he owns mines and factories. At its peak, his game studio employed more than 500 people; it now maintains a staff of around 400.
“Once you pay him today, you probably won’t see him for the next week,” Brother Bao said. “Chances are he’ll be out drinking. I don’t dare buy too many cell phones—who knows if there’ll be fifty people in line today and a hundred who don’t show up tomorrow? It’s just too unpredictable.”
As someone who has spent the first half of his life struggling, Brother Zhong needs time to adapt to and understand the local culture.
He ran a home appliance retail business in Weinan City, Shaanxi Province. In 1999, his small 100-square-meter store generated 18 million yuan in retail sales, and Zhu Jianghong, the founder of Gree Electric Appliances, personally visited the store.Later, he partnered with Yulin Mobile to run a promotional campaign, signing up 10,000 users in just ten days. Through a promotion that offered home appliances as gifts for prepaid phone credits, he gave away a full shipping container’s worth of microwave ovens.Later still, he purchased more than 8,000 square meters of real estate to build a hotel and entered the cryptocurrency “mining” industry—until 2021, when the National Development and Reform Commission issued a notice cracking down on cryptocurrency mining activities, causing his “mining” business to collapse.
“My life has been too smooth so far,” Brother Zhong said. It was precisely because things had gone so smoothly that he fell into the trap of arrogance. After the mining industry collapsed, doing business in China became increasingly difficult. Approaching sixty, Brother Zhong refused to accept his fate. “I’ve spent my whole life looking for opportunities.If you tell me to accept my fate and stop looking for opportunities, I’ll get so bored I’ll go stir-crazy.”
In 2024, he set off for Madagascar. This island nation, which consistently ranks near the bottom of the global GDP rankings, has extremely low labor costs, is free from large-scale warfare, is surrounded by the ocean on all sides, and is relatively more open than the African interior. Brother Zhong hoped to find a path to “renewal” here.At first, he made raffia bags and wool scarves, but last summer, when he returned to China and chatted with his second son—who was still in college—about a game called *Operation Delta*, Brother Zhong’s interest was piqued again. “Twenty million daily active users—that big? I said I had to study this and get a thorough grasp of it.”
After doing some research, Brother Zhong quickly found a new direction for himself: opening a game power-leveling studio in Africa.
02
Cultural Conflict
Zhong Ge refers to Madagascar as his “place of rebirth,” and he has high hopes for this studio’s business.
There used to be a note on the workshop wall that read, “Heaven rewards diligence.” Brother Zhong tried to use these words to convey to the workers the principle that the more you work, the more you earn, but he later discovered that this classical Chinese wisdom didn’t take root in Madagascar: “The Malagasy people understand ‘Heaven,’ but they don’t understand ‘rewarding diligence.’”
Of course, there were a few employees who took his words to heart and shared them with their families when they got home. Upon hearing this, their parents—unlike Chinese parents—didn’t feel pleased; instead, they asked their children, “Son, or daughter, why have you become so dim-witted since you started working at that Chinese company?”
Zhong Ge gradually came to realize that the problem wasn’t with the workers, but rather the cultural gap between the two civilizations. Madagascar has long been in a transitional phase from a tribal society to an industrial one, and “people generally lack a sense of what it means to go to work.”
This characteristic of tribal civilization naturally fosters greater solidarity among workers and carries a certain degree of exclusivity.
“They, in turn, look down on us,” Brother Zhong said, “thinking we’re just like ants—all we care about is making money; we’re purely economic creatures.”
But Brother Zhong does not believe that Africans are inherently “lazy,”In his view, behind the workers’ various behaviors lie not only the protection afforded by their uniquely favorable natural conditions but also the lingering traces of poverty caused by failed governance. They lack an understanding of business and the workplace, nor do they have the conditions necessary to develop such an understanding. In Brother Zhong’s view, this cannot be attributed to the workers themselves.
Brother Bao has a different perspective on these cultural differences. He employs more than 400 workers locally and has concluded that there is a significant gap in efficiency compared to China: “When one person is working, there might be eight others standing around watching; their efficiency is roughly one-tenth that of Chinese workers.”However, he doesn’t dwell on whether to adapt to or change this culture: “If someone is hard to manage, just fire them—you won’t give them a second chance.”
In contrast, Brother Zhong prefers to build rapport with the workers. He conducted a survey specifically to ask the workers why they applied for the job—in other words, what drew them there? Was it to earn money or to have fun? The results surprised him: nearly 70 percent of the workers were there to play games for free, while only 30 percent were there to earn a wage.
Brother Zhong and the Workers
Now that several months have passed, workers have come and gone, and gradually a core group of veteran workers who stay at the studio long-term has emerged. Brother Zhong’s answer to this question has also changed. The last time he asked, the ratio had shifted to fifty-fifty, which made Brother Zhong quite pleased. “I think they’re being sincere,” he said.
As a result, the lives of the young people who stayed to work have also improved.
Brother Zhong once asked the workers how they spent their wages. The vast majority said they would prioritize improving their living conditions—for example, by buying a cell phone. Since Brother Zhong runs a business selling used cell phones, he naturally became the workers’ supplier. “It’s a kind of closed loop: when you get paid, you come to us, and we sell you a cell phone at a price lower than the market rate—and that way, we get our money back.”
Young people also buy secondhand Chinese sneakers or a full set of athletic wear—items that were previously out of their reach. As for the money they have left over, some workers save it for their own tuition, while others give it to their parents to help improve their family’s overall standard of living.
“These kids are still mostly good-hearted,” said Brother Zhong, who was also pleased to see the workers able to support their families. Inspired by these workers, more and more young people have been coming to his studio hoping to apply for jobs, including relatives, friends, and classmates of the current workers. “It’s a different experience from working at a foreign company.”
03
Ideals and Reality
In Madagascar, young people don’t have a very fulfilling life.
Mobile internet, which has long been widespread in China, is a luxury for young people there. Baobao Ge estimates that while the local smartphone penetration rate is reportedly 30 percent, less than 5 percent of users actually have internet access. “It’s like everyone can afford to buy a car but can’t afford to fill it up with gas.”
Zhong Ge has also noticed this. In the homes of the vast majority of workers who come to his studio, it’s not that there’s no electricity, but there are “daily power outages,” and the internet is even more unaffordable.A 250GB data plan on a one-year contract costs over 300 yuan per month—equivalent to an average person’s monthly income. If, like the studio, they were to purchase data on an ad hoc basis, it would cost between 800 and 1,000 yuan per month.
Although the area is poor, local prices are shockingly high. A bucket of bottled water in the office costs 45 yuan, a bowl of beef noodle soup costs 38 yuan—and if you add an egg, it’s over 40 yuan—and electricity costs a little over 2 yuan per kilowatt-hour.The unstable power supply is also a problem for all kinds of home appliances. As Brother Zhong puts it, “If you buy a computer, the power supply will blow within a week; if you buy a TV, it’ll break within a month or two.”
Of course, the vast majority of local households don’t face this kind of problem. After all, a GeForce 1060 graphics card that costs less than 2,000 yuan in China goes for 4,700 in Malaysia, and an LCD monitor that costs 170 yuan in China sells for 680 in Malaysia.
To keep the studio running, Brother Zhong had no choice but to install a solar power system himself to solve the power supply problem, and Brother Baobao also spent 50,000 yuan to install a solar power system with energy storage.
With limited access to electricity and the internet, local workers didn’t have many opportunities to play games before landing this job. The vast majority of workers still use basic feature phones or second- or third-hand used phones from China that can only be used for making calls.
There were also early versions of internet cafes in the area—small “arcades” with two or three computers. If they had controllers in addition to the computers, that was considered a luxury setup. Most of the time, the scene in these small internet cafes was one or two people playing, while the remaining seven or eight stood around watching to get their fix.
The vast majority of young people don’t have the means to keep playing games after they get off work at the studio. “He can’t afford it himself, so no matter how much he loves it, there’s nothing he can do,” Brother Zhong said with a smile, adding, “After playing games all day and working ten hours, you’re already so exhausted you feel like throwing up.”
Brother Baobao had another observation about the local youth’s leisure activities: they have almost no ways to entertain themselves, and some even get so bored that they play in the mud. Consequently, local teenagers generally start dating at a younger age. “What can you do? There’s nothing else to do,” he said.
Street scenes in Madagascar photographed by Brother Zhong, showing young people playing soccer
The lack of material and spiritual enrichment does not mean that local young people lack their own thoughts and ideas; on the contrary, Zhong Ge found that these young people have an accurate understanding of the current state of the country. “Actually, they’re quite clear-headed; they’re an awakened generation.”
Brother Zhong once asked more than twenty young people in his studio a big question: Are you optimistic or pessimistic about the country’s future? In Brother Zhong’s view, although Madagascar is underdeveloped, this also means there is a vast market and plenty of opportunities to explore. So he asked the question expecting them to answer optimistically, but to his surprise,these workers unanimously stated that they were not optimistic about their country. When Brother Zhong pressed them for the reason, they replied, “Corruption in the government.”
Just like young people anywhere else in the world, these local workers look forward to seeing the wider world and making a difference in it.
In Brother Zhong’s workshop, there are quite a few local college students from Madagascar, including several who are studying Chinese, as well as others studying German and learning how to install plumbing and electrical systems.Brother Zhong’s interpreter said he plans to go to China in the future. When Brother Zhong asked him which city he’d like to visit once he gets there, the young man didn’t mention tourist destinations like Beijing or Shanghai—instead, he said he wanted to go to Guangzhou and Yiwu. “He just wants to bring goods from there back to make money.”
China’s prosperity has caught Africa’s attention, a fact that makes Brother Zhong proud: “Chinese translation, Chinese studies, and the Chinese language have all become quite prestigious here.”
For these college students who are planning their future careers, working at Chinese game-boosting studios is a great opportunity that allows them to afford their tuition.In Madagascar, the path to college for the vast majority of ordinary people is fraught with obstacles. They typically take one year off after each year of study to work and save money, then return to school for another year. As a result, many students end up taking six or seven years to complete a three-year college program.
But Brother Zhong plans to reduce the number of college graduates he hires because these students—who are too smart and too idealistic—don’t stay long. “As soon as they start making money, they go back to school, which is really a hassle for us.”
04
The Charger and God
Zhong Ge’s studio doesn’t welcome another kind of “smart” person either.
He once had a worker whom clients called a “genius with an IQ of 160.” In order to reach the required transaction amount—that is, the number of Haf coins, the virtual currency in *Operation Delta*—faster, this worker secretly split up the bullets in the account owner’s warehouse and resold them.Originally packed in slots of sixty rounds each, the ammunition was split into slots of thirty rounds for resale. It wasn’t until the system automatically consolidated the slots that the account owner realized something was missing.
The employee’s “creative idea” left the account owner speechless. The account owner joked that Brother Zhong absolutely had to keep this worker on, but Brother Zhong fired him on the spot. “I wouldn’t dare keep someone like that for even a single day. If he pulled a stunt like that on you, it would cost me at least a few million Haf coins in compensation.If he ever turned on me, a fool like me wouldn’t stand a chance.”
In fact, minor administrative hiccups like this are not uncommon in Brother Zhong’s studio.
The translator once told Brother Zhong that out of the forty people in the studio, as many as thirty-five might be thinking of stealing his stuff. This isn’t an exaggeration—once, Brother Zhong had just received a shipment of mice and headphones that had been flown in, and he excitedly went to show them to the workers. But by the end of the workday, the equipment had been “purchased for free.”
Baobao Ge has also experienced Madagascar’s unique local customs and social environment firsthand. Having spent many years doing business in Africa, he’s grown accustomed to being robbed and mugged. According to him, the most dangerous moment he faced was when “bandits pointed a gun at his head.”
But certain events revealed another side of the locals to Brother Zhong.
Brother Zhong recalled that two chargers had once gone missing from his studio. They were 25-watt and 40-watt fast chargers bought in Huaqiangbei—items the local workers couldn’t afford on their own. Brother Zhong brought up the incident at the next day’s meeting, but instead of framing it as a disciplinary issue, he approached it from a different angle: “As for the chargers, I don’t care—they’re not expensive.But once you steal them, your manager—Ma Guo’s manager—will have to compensate me. His wife just gave birth to a baby who isn’t even a month old yet; this is exactly when he needs money the most. By stealing a charger, aren’t you putting him in a difficult situation?”
Then he added, “Don’t you people always say, ‘Malaysians should help Malaysians’? You stole it from him, and now he has to compensate me—so how is that helping a fellow Malaysian? And God is in heaven—would He allow you to do this? You go to church every Sunday—would God allow you to do this?”
These words had an immediate effect; the very next day after the meeting, the two stolen chargers were sitting on the desk.
In Brother Zhong’s view, the fact that these two chargers were lost and then recovered sheds some light on the situation: “Even though he’s poor and likes to steal, it’s still because he’s poor—but he has a good heart.” He paused for a moment, then posed a question: “Think about it—if this had happened in China, who would have cared about you?Who would listen to your lectures? Who would even return them to you? You’d be over the moon.”
Workers in the Workshop and Work Records
Despite encountering all sorts of management issues, Brother Zhong still prefers to focus on the workers’ strengths; he believes that the root cause of many problems does not lie with the workers themselves. “These are different people shaped by different cultures.”
Sometimes, this complex kind of “simplicity” brings him some pleasant surprises.
As a result of intensified domestic crackdowns and transnational joint operations, telecommunications fraud rings that had been based in Southeast Asia have been steadily relocating in recent years, with some moving to Madagascar. The profiles of the telecommunications fraud operatives these rings are trying to recruit locally closely match the workers needed by Brother Zhong’s studio:young, computer-literate, familiar with the internet, fast typists, and quick thinkers.
Simply put, they also need the brightest young people.
Zhong Ge admitted that the salaries offered by telecom fraud rings are much higher than those at gaming studios, but he found that many young people are unwilling to take those jobs. “These kids are Christians, and they know deep down that this is a sin.” In contrast, although the pay at gaming studios isn’t as high, “he has a clear conscience.He knows he hasn’t harmed anyone.”
Moreover, objectively speaking, these young people who are willing to stay in the studio and play games for more than ten hours a day aren’t really lazy. Although their efficiency in mining HAV coins doesn’t match that of studios in China—which routinely exceed 25 million—and their daily output is only around 15 million, in Brother Zhong’s eyes, that’s already pretty good.
Not to mention that the vast majority of these young people had never played video games before and had to start from scratch; even the local network connection to the Chinese servers alone limited their efficiency. Fiber-optic cables that stretch across half the globe result in a latency of nearly 500 milliseconds. As Brother Zhong put it, “‘By the time you hear the gunshot, you’re already dead. When have Chinese kids ever played games like this?’”
Even with a production capacity of 15 million Haf coins, the output value would still be considerable once scale is achieved.Brother Baobao has done the math: based on 15 million per person, the output value per shift can reach 30 yuan; for a 24-hour period, that’s 60 yuan. With 50 workers, the total monthly output value comes to nearly 90,000 yuan.
05
The Risks of “Gold Rush”
It’s not just the telecom fraud parks that are poaching employees from Brother Zhong’s studio; an increasing number of Chinese people are also flocking to the “run-and-steal” business in Africa.
When Brother Zhong and his son discovered this business opportunity, the market was still a blue ocean. At the time, Brother Zhong analyzed the situation: “Rich people don’t understand Africa, nor do they understand games. As for people who understand games, they only know how to play—not how to make money.As for those running game studios, they’re unaware of the labor cost differences in Africa. And those who’ve established a foothold in Africa don’t understand games. This created a knowledge gap, which is why this relatively small niche went largely unnoticed.”
That assessment was correct at the time, but in the Information Age, information gaps never last very long.
Brother Baobao’s experience confirms this trend. He posted a video about African game studios, “which went viral overnight, racking up 20 million views, and lots of people reached out to me wanting to get into this business.” But this was followed by a flood of copycats, and in just one year, “over a hundred studios across Africa went out of business.”
Faced with intensifying competition, “Brother Baobao” is planning to pivot toward running a platform. He intends to consolidate all domestic and international game power-leveling services in Africa and seek partnerships with major Chinese companies. Of course, this path also means more headaches: “If I were to go back to China now to build systems, do R&D, develop software, and create apps, I wouldn’t know where to start.”
Zhong Ge, however, takes a very matter-of-fact view of the intensifying competition: “This is something that is beyond human control. Labor will naturally flow to areas where labor costs are lower—this is an irreversible trend.”
But coming to Africa to “strike it rich” is far from as simple as spotting information gaps. Brother Zhong believes that the real test here isn’t your business acumen, but whether you can withstand cultural conflicts in employee management, the widespread lack of infrastructure, and the ever-present security risks.
In the second half of last year, a coup took place in Madagascar—the most significant upheaval in decades—which ultimately resulted in the military seizing power and the ouster of the former president.In the early days of the unrest, Wealth Plaza—owned by a prominent Chinese businessman—was surrounded and looted by tens of thousands of people. Brother Zhong still remembers the scene: “After the merchandise had been completely looted, those who arrived later began smashing tiles and pulling out electrical wires, carrying off everything in sight—shelves, light fixtures, and more. Finally, when there was truly nothing left,they set Wealth Plaza on fire.”
That night, he could hear the sound of AK-47 gunfire coming from outside from time to time.The next morning, Brother Zhong stepped out of his home and saw three bodies about 300 meters away. In December, a Chinese couple who had lived in Malaysia for over a decade was brutally murdered in their home. “It wasn’t until four days later, when the stench of their decomposing bodies wafted out, that neighbors discovered them.”
Brother Zhong on the Streets of Madagascar
Zhong Ge said that these are all “probabilistic events”—not everyone will encounter them, but if you do, it means it’s all over. Zhong Ge can’t do much about it; all he can do is strengthen his security measures. He lives in a villa in an affluent neighborhood, surrounded by high walls topped with barbed wire and guarded by professional security personnel.
In Madagascar, he doesn’t have much of a nightlife; every day after work, he goes straight home and bolts the door. Brother Zhong jokingly refers to his place as a “little prison”: “Once it gets dark, you just settle in quietly.”
When discussing the local business environment, Baobao pointed out another issue that Chinese people often overlook: the government’s attitude.Unlike local governments in China, which are busy attracting investment, doing business here requires a different approach to managing relationships with local authorities: “No matter how many young people you hire or how many jobs you create for them, you have to pay them money—otherwise, they won’t let you operate.”
06
It’s all just a phase
As more and more African knife-making workshops emerge, discussions about them on domestic social media platforms are becoming increasingly lively.
But these discussions aren’t necessarily just about novelty. Brother Zhong sometimes comes across overly sensationalized comments that make him feel uneasy—such as people joking about “electric batons,” directly referring to these workers as “cyber slaves,” or making other discriminatory remarks.
Zhong Ge knows that when more people pay attention and discuss something, it naturally brings traffic benefits. “The short-term benefits are definitely there—it’s attracted domestic attention and become a hot topic, a trend, and a buzzword that everyone is talking about.”
In the age of the “eyeball economy,” popularity translates into more orders and revenue. Yet Brother Zhong believes that the downsides of this kind of traffic outweigh the benefits; when people enthusiastically share and consume those terrible jokes based on stereotypes, they are essentially reinforcing existing prejudices.
This is Brother Zhong’s favorite photo; he says it looks “full of youth and vitality.”
Sometimes, when the comments in the livestream go too far with their jokes, Brother Zhong can’t hold back his anger and snaps back, “While you’re making fun of them, if you were to compare yourselves in soccer, dancing, or long-distance running, you wouldn’t even be fit to tie their shoes.”
Brother Zhong had mixed feelings toward these young people, who were about the same age as his youngest son. He sensed the natural cultural divide between them and was troubled by the strike and everyday management conflicts, but he also saw in them kindness and a vision for a better future.
During the interview, Brother Zhong emphasized more than once that the perceptions people in China have of these young Africans—whether it’s that they’re lazy, unfamiliar with things like video games, or prone to theft and robbery—are all deeply rooted in the poor socioeconomic conditions in their home countries, rather than being the fault of any individual. In his view, people are the same no matter what country or region they come from.“We should view everyone with an eye of equality. Everyone comes into this world for a time, and everyone deserves to live a good life. There’s no need to look down on anyone.”

title: 《黎明行者之血》：全世界游戏行业倒退十年，而我保持不变
text:
2015年《巫师3》横扫各大游戏界年度奖项时，彼时的Konrad Tomaszkiewicz正坐在游戏总监的位置上。后来他又深度参与了《赛博朋克2077》，在CDPR一待就是十几年。
多年后，他离开了这家让他功成名就的公司，拉上一众《巫师3》《赛博朋克2077》时期的老同事，成立了Rebel Wolves。同年，网易以少数股权战略投资入局——Konrad在官宣里说道：“我们选择网易，是因为对方聊的是游戏本身，而不只是利润数字。”
“原班人马出走创业”这个剧本，这些年我们已经听了太多。他们其中的多数都走上了“开头豪言壮语，发售沉默不语，售后胡言乱语”的路子。所以从本作公布的那天起，玩家们的心情与其说是期待，不如说是戒备：精神续作？《巫师3》的《心之眼》罢了。
是吸血鬼，也是家人侠
我不知道有多少玩家同我一样，在上手本作的主角科恩时的第一步就是找一个七八米高的山坡往下跳，来测试本作主角的“易碎程度”。毕竟它的老前辈杰洛特是个从台阶上跳下来就会崴脚的老东西。
《黎明行者之血》将游戏的舞台设置在了14世纪前后的欧洲。彼时的欧洲大陆被战争搅成了一锅粥，而黑死病的爆发又对战争的幸存者们进行了一波收割，人类社会迎来了前所未有的虚弱。而对于在世界背面蛰伏许久的吸血鬼们，这无疑是最好的出山时机了。
吸血鬼文学最早可追溯至18世纪的民俗传说，并在19世纪的欧洲通俗文学领域迎来鼎盛时期。值得一提的是，诗人拜伦的私人医生约翰·威廉·波利多里在1819年发布的短篇小说《吸血鬼》通常被认定为是英文文学史上吸血鬼文学的滥觞。
在游戏的开篇CG里你能看到，主角科恩为了保护染疫的妹妹不受军队的绞杀，被迫与吸血鬼们达成交易。而科恩原本只是村里一个普通年轻人，在家乡被血族攻占后，他在一连串意外里被卷入血祭仪式，成了一种叫“黎明行者”的存在。而你的家人被吸血鬼领主布兰西斯掳走，而留给他的时间，只有30天。
不过在成为"黎明行者"之前，科恩首先是儿子、是哥哥、是家里的壮劳力。父亲是个退役的雇佣兵，严厉沉默，是家里的顶梁柱；母亲则被一次次献血彻底拖垮，整日浑浑噩噩，得靠村里药剂师配的药才能短暂清醒。所以游戏开场你干的活是这样的：劈柴、生火、给母亲喂饭、跑腿抓药。相比于其他动作游戏的打打杀杀，成为黎明行者的第一步得先完成家里的一摞家务——"家人侠"三个字，科恩当之无愧。
时间不在于你拥有多少，而在于你怎样使用
塞内卡在《论生命之短暂》里说："我们并非拥有的时间太少，而是浪费的时间太多。"这话放在《黎明行者之血》里，或许得反过来读。
当你打通序章之后，游戏时间线里距离布兰西斯的加冕仪式便只剩下了30天。每个白天和夜晚各分成8个时间段。推进任务要消耗时间——做一次调查大约耗1格，清一个据点大约3格，重要的抉择和行动则花得更多。
在这30天里几乎没有传统意义上的"主线"。目标只有一个：救出家人。山谷里散落着质量参差但时常有惊喜的支线，其中好几条都能一步步把你引向最终决战——每完成一条重要的前置支线抑或是清除一个据点，你就能获得一些新方式来协助你对敌。
游戏中还存在着一套“宫廷系统”，你可以粗暴地把它理解成你的通缉星级。布兰西斯的统治依赖麾下几个瓦莱克西封臣，你清据点、撕旗帜，毁坏供血站等都会提升你的恶名度。恶名度共分九级，每一级的提升都会使得布兰西斯宫廷颁布一条全新的法令，诸如在地图定居点内增派巡逻、上涨物价、加强NPC等一系列手段让你的探索更为困难。当你解锁恶名度到一定程度，你就可以前往地区领主的所在地挑战它的“权威”。如若你能够提前将其斩于马下，在最终决战时你或许就能少面对一个难题。
回到每一个打完序章的玩家都想要追问的问题：30天，够用吗？
实际体验下来，它比大部分人想的都要宽松些。只要你不成心在山谷里闲逛一辈子，正常在地图上清据点、做任务，时间基本都够用。这套时间系统存在的最大意义并不是让你感到紧迫，而是让你自己在“鱼”和“熊掌”中做出选择。哪怕时间耗尽也并不意味着游戏结束，而是将你的故事导向另一种结局。
但“宽松”也不等于“随便”。这款游戏的时间安排还是相当有策略纵深在里面的：什么事白天做、什么事晚上做，哪条线先推、哪条点后推，都会切身地影响你的游戏进程。有些支线甚至是带“保鲜期”的，你去晚了，赶到现场时人已经没了。对全收集、全成就的玩家来说，如果你错过了，可能就得开二周目了；而对普通玩家来说，规划路线、安排日程、然后为自己的安排承担后果，这或许就是这套系统提供的核心乐趣。
当然，这套30天的系统本身就为多周目游玩提供了相当大的乐趣。
比时间系统更值得说的，其实还是撑起它的叙事结构。本作采用了网状叙事的叙事方式。游戏的支线并不是主线的点缀，它本身就是通往结局的助力。玩家所结交的势力、扳倒的封臣、做过的每个关键抉择，都会在这张网上牵出新的线头，最终汇成专属于你的那条复仇之路。
任务完成的先后顺序、过程中的具体取舍，都会在这张超大的叙事网上激起真实的涟漪。这种“网状叙事”让每一周目都带着强烈的个人印记：同一个游戏，你和朋友的存档聊到后期，很可能已经是两个完全不同的故事。
旧瓶装新酒还是老调重弹？
游戏中共有三套技能树，分别为巫术、剑术与血族技能，即吸血鬼形态下的技能。
你需要通过角色等级的提升获得技能点数，并前往散落在地图四处的神龛进行加点，来不断提升自己的性能。
本作战斗的核心是一套方向判定系统。敌人的攻击分上、下、左、右四个方向，你需要观察起手方向，做出对应的格挡或者闪避。格挡方向错了也能免伤、只消耗耐力。而如果正确格挡后，你可以对敌人使出相当致命的一击，并且接上你的连段。敌人的致命一击落下前会有瞬间提示，抓住那一帧完成闪避，对方会踉跄一两秒。你大可以抓住这个机会对敌人补刀。
这套战斗系统并非由本作首创，你可以很清楚地一窥到它的灵感来源。《天国：拯救》系列里的方向博弈、《荣耀战魂》的格挡节奏，都可以算是它的近亲。它没有走时下流行的魂西"翻滚蹭刀"路线，它更鼓励你在敌人攻击的间隙勇敢进攻，在攻守兼备中完成斩杀。
和他的老大哥《巫师3》比起来，本作的战斗系统已经可以说是进步十足了。相比于杰洛特的招牌拜年剑法，胜负不再单单取决于数值，同样也依靠上了对决博弈。作为玩家口中最大的短板，《巫师3》的战斗在《黎明行者之血》中得到了相当好的补足与呈现。
当然，这套战斗系统说起来简单，就好像只教会了你加法交换律，却要你去解微积分一样。
游戏中有大量的对群场景，你在战斗中不仅仅需要面对锁定系统为你提供的敌人，你还需要时刻提防镜头外突如其来的刀刃，在方向提示出现的一瞬间完成抵御。
什么？科恩你也要打十个？！
笔者曾经在一个营地中向面前的两个士兵“勇敢地”发出挑衅，但随即而来的就是莫名其妙地从四周站起来十来号人拿着各式武器将我团团围住，最后将我乱棍打死。
十年之期已到
显而易见的是，本作仍有不少令人忍俊不禁的瑕疵。
当你帮助村民干活时，进入对话框时他们会恭恭敬敬地向你表达感谢；而你一旦退出对话框，不小心撞到他们时，你仍会受到他们最热烈的怒骂。
没解锁变狼形态的科恩几乎只能用坐11路公交车，用双脚丈量大地。即使可以借助神龛的力量，在地图内的神龛快速旅行，但中途的赶路过程仍让人感到有些折磨。
在序章的某个支线任务中，当你在洞窟里听闻那个亟需被你拯救的人说道洞窟深处有极为恐怖的声音出现，作为一介凡人的你——起码在游戏开头你看上去并没有太多的异能，你的第一直觉不是原路返回，将人安安全全带回，而是深入虎谭，带着一个拖油瓶硬刚远古怪物。
这种勇气和莽撞似乎如同一种谶言一般，印证在这一批创作者们的身上。
从2015年到2026年，游戏行业飞速发展的十多年。开放世界游戏成了游戏工业里的流水线。玩家的任务清单越拉越长，地图越铺越大；服务型游戏你方唱罢我登场，3A的预算翻了几番，游戏质量却远不如从前。
游戏的生产者们已经学会了怎么把游戏越做越大，但是好像逐渐忽视了把游戏越做越精。
《黎明行者之血》当然不完美。它粗粝，它执拗，它在不少地方都仍带着新工作室首部作品的青涩，如同刚化身吸血鬼的科恩初入世一样。但当整个行业都在向前着一条道路狂奔的时候，他们选择驻足原地，回望过去，订制着修正那个时代下，游戏创作者们路线的舆图。

title: 腾讯又将测试一款SLG，有立体地形和滑索功能
text:
腾讯又将测试一款SLG，有立体地形和滑索功能
游戏新知君
2026-09-08 19:18 发布于 湖北 游戏新知官方账号
关注
腾讯最近在为一款 SLG 《代号：争锋》 招募测试玩家。本次测试为线上保密测试，将于9月下旬进行。
结合现有公开信息，猜测该游戏可能就是此前曝光的 《代号：大战术》 ，据称核心玩法类似于 《重返帝国》 ，也因此被网友视为 「《重返帝国2》」 。《代号：大战术》主打多文明策略，去年9月曾开启招募测试，今年4月更名为 《代号：统帅》 并再次招募玩家，原计划在次月进行，但后续因「重大更新将至」而取消了测试。
《代号：争锋》是一款华夏题材的 国战SLG 。据介绍，本作实装了众多华夏传奇名将，供玩家自由招募、组建专属军团。玩家将建造城池，研习科技，训练士兵。同时，游戏主打 5V5可视化战斗 ，简化了战后信息，让玩家对战况一目了然。
比较特别的是，游戏还设计了立体地形并添加了滑索功能。地形有高低差，可借助滑索飞渡到目的地。玩家还可与盟友合作，建造各式奇特的攻防设施，用工事牵制敌军。

title: 字节在开发新AI模型，可为游戏创建虚拟世界
text:
字节在开发新AI模型，可为游戏创建虚拟世界
游戏新知君
2026-09-08 19:18 发布于 湖北 游戏新知官方账号
关注
问AI  ·  该模型作为“飞轮”如何串联字节多线业务？
据彭博社报道，字节跳动正在开发一款实时生成空间视频的AI模型，预计最快会在下个月正式推出。该模型基于 Seedance （字节已经发布的AI视频生成大模型） 构建，支持用户为直播、短剧和游戏创建可交互的虚拟世界。这也意味着，字节将杀入机器人技术与自治系统领域，与Meta、Alphabet展开正面竞争。
报道称，字节希望通过公司在视频领域的顶尖技术积累，借着这款最新AI模型，将公司送入蓬勃发展的「 世界模型 」赛道。字节正在将大量B2B业务转向视频制作与生成。
知情人士称，字节将该 空间视频模型 视为驱动整个生态的「飞轮 （Flywheel） 」：它能让用户置身于三维世界中，功能类似于谷歌的 Genie ，将字节的AI模型、云计算资源、内容平台以及扩展现实业务 Pico 串联起来。今年年初，谷歌推出 Genie 3 ，允许用户与实时渲染的虚拟世界进行交互。
若进展顺利，这款新模型或将为字节与Meta、苹果的竞争中开辟出新战场。Meta与苹果都在虚拟现实和混合现实领域投入了大量资金，但时至今日双方的豪赌都还不太明朗。
据称，字节新模型追求的目标，包括生成能响应Pico用户语音指令或动作的虚拟世界。其中一位知情人士称，该模型能以约0.05秒延迟、20帧/秒的速度提供点播视频。它试图将空间内容生成这一计算密集型过程转移到云端，从而降低VR设备的前期成本。这将减少头显所需的计算能力，为更廉价、更轻量化的硬件铺路。

title: 《旅行青蛙》停运冲上热搜第六，游戏已经下架
text:
《旅行青蛙》停运冲上热搜第六，游戏已经下架
游戏新知君
2026-09-08 19:18 发布于 湖北 游戏新知官方账号
关注
问AI  ·  团队不足五人凭爱熬着，旅行青蛙如何维系情怀？
今日 （9月8日） ， 灵犀互娱 代理的《 旅行青蛙·中国之旅 》发布公告称，由于IP授权合作到期，游戏将于2026年12月8日正式停运。消息传出后引发全网热议，#旅行青蛙相关话题登上热搜榜，勾起了无数网友的回忆。
《旅行青蛙》于2018年引进中国大陆，曾在全网掀起十分火爆的「养蛙」热潮。作为一款轻量级休闲产品，其长线生命力也是比较少见的。尽管随着时间的推移，游戏热度开始下滑，但IP至今都还有一定的影响力。
不过也因为商业化表现并不突出，《旅行青蛙》曾多次传出停运消息。
2024年，游戏便曾短暂下架小程序，之后运营方表示为缩减运营成本「放生」人工客服，项目组剩余不到5人。运营方还曾回复玩家称「一直以来都是白打工的状态，全凭对呱呱的爱熬着了」。2025年，游戏 VIVO渠道服 停运，再度引发玩家担忧，冲上热搜，官方还专门出来安抚玩家。而从今年6月1日起，《旅行青蛙》官方小红书账号就没有更新动态了。这一次，玩家等来了停运公告。
这些年也不是没有人模仿这只青蛙，但《旅行青蛙》的成功很难复制。灵犀互娱就曾推出一款类似玩法的「养崽」游戏《 花花与幕间剧 》。后者采用舞台剧团的题材，画风也很治愈唯美，可惜无论是人气还是流水都是一般，已于今年3月宣布停止内容更新 （服务器保留） ，官方账号也停更至今。
/   END   /

title: Capcom says it will focus on reviving dormant IPs after Onimusha: Way of the Sword's breakout launch
text:
Capcom has revealed it will focus on reactivating dormant intellectual property following a strong launch for Onimusha: Way of the Sword.
Way of the Sword is the series' first mainline entry in more than two decades. It sold more than 1 million copies worldwide on launch day, September 4, taking the Onimusha franchise's lifetime sales past 10 million units since it began in 2001.
Capcom said pre-release demos and hands-on showcases had helped build awareness among a broad range of players ahead of launch.
"In addition to regularly releasing major new titles each year, Capcom is focusing on re-activating IPs that haven't had a new title launch recently," the company said , adding that it intends to "further maximize corporate value" by drawing on its back catalog.
Capcom used almost identical language in a December 2024 investor release tied to the games' reveal, and told investors as far back as 2019 that unlocking value from its older IP was part of its long-term plans.
Way of the Sword casts players as Miyamoto Musashi in Edo-era Kyoto and is out now on Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

title: Don't Nod warns it may not have enough funding to operate beyond January 2027
text:
Don't Nod has warned there is "material uncertainty" over its ability to continue operating beyond January 31, 2027, unless it secures further external financing.
The warning came alongside the French publisher and developer's first-half 2026 results and further detail on a restructuring plan first announced on September 1.
Gross cash fell from $17.9 million (€15.4 million) at the end of 2025 to $11.4 million (€9.8 million) at the end of June 2026, and $9.3 million (€8 million) by the end of July.
Don't Nod's total operating revenue, which includes capitalized production costs, fell 56% year-over-year to $7.1 million (€6.1 million), down from $16.2 million (€13.9 million).
The company also said neither its sci-fi adventure game Aphelion nor an unannounced project, internally referred to as P14, met the funding-capacity criteria required, despite what it described as expressions of interest.
Revenue alone, covering sales and development work, fell 14% to $7.1 million (€6.1 million) from $8.1 million (€7 million), with sales declining to $4.1 million (€3.5 million) and development revenue rising to $3 million (€2.6 million), largely driven by a Montreal-based narrative game based on a "major" Netflix property. Operating EBITDA loss widened to $5 million (€4.3 million), from $2.3 million (€2 million) in the same period last year.
As part of its restructuring, Don't Nod said it is "refocusing its operations in France around a single production line, bringing together the expertise required to launch new projects before the completion of current productions."
The company said a transformation project under consideration could lead to the reduction of up to 90 positions in France. The board approved the plan on September 4, and initial talks with employee representatives and union negotiations have begun.
CEO Oskar Guilbert said the results "confirm the major challenges facing our industry," adding: "The measures being considered today are difficult; we fully appreciate what they may mean for the employees affected and are ensuring that the necessary support measures are put in place."
This isn't the first warning over Don't Nod's finances this year. GamesIndustry.biz reported in June that the company's auditors had warned it could run out of cash by November 2026 without further financing, after Tencent, Don't Nod's largest shareholder, declined a request for a short-term capital increase.
The company also cut an unspecified number of jobs in 2025 following an earlier restructuring around three genres: RPG, narrative adventure, and action adventure.

title: Arm explains its mobile-first AI-reconstruction technology, which takes a different tack from the "black box" approach of DLSS 5
text:
Today, the British semiconductor and software design company Arm is holding the Arm Everywhere China event in Shanghai to unveil its latest contributions to the AI computing landscape.
The company's aim is to provide a full ecosystem for AI-native computing, including the new AI-native compute platform CSS for Mobile 2, as well as the Arm Mali G2-Ultra NX GPU – a new chip built around neural computing, which promises improved graphics performance at a much lower cost in terms of heat and power consumption. Arm claims its on-device AI will boost graphical performance via a method it positions as more open than Nvidia's divisive DLSS 5 technology, and closer to the developers' original vision.
The firm would not confirm which devices will be using the Mali G2-Ultra NX GPU, but the earlier Mali G1-Ultra chip is found in devices from Xiaomi, Vivo, and OnePlus.
Deyan Lazarov is in Arm's GPU product team as part of the Edge AI business unit, which deals with consumer devices like phones, tablets, laptops, and consoles. He says Arm has been working on the Mali G2-Ultra NX for the past two and a half years, and the thinking behind the chip is to allow mobile developers to take advantage of compute-intensive technology like ray tracing.
"There was actually growing adoption of ray tracing in mobile titles," he says. "The technology has been a bit slow to get going, but now we're seeing more and more titles actually interested in enabling ray tracing."
As GamesIndustry.biz reported earlier this year , the new GPU allows mobile developers to take advantage of Unreal Engine technologies such as MegaLights, and Arm has worked with Sumo Digital to create the game Neural Dawn, which showcases the power of the Mali G2-Ultra NX.
Neural Dawn, developed with Sumo Digital, offers a showcase of Arm's technology | Image credit: Sumo Digital/Arm
Lazarov says the chip is aimed to support titles that are "mobile first, but then they want to look great: they want to look like desktop titles."
"Then we also have other titles which are just cross-platform by design, so you can play them on pretty much any gaming device that you have. And then those types of titles naturally want to provide a unified experience to their players, so that when you're gaming on your console at home, and then you jump on a train to London or whatever, you don't get a significant drop in the experience."
A few of the games that will be taking advantage of the power of the new chip include Arena Breakout Infinite from Tencent, Where Winds Meet from NetEase, and Infinity Nikki from Infold Games.
Too hot to handle
"The thing that's different about mobile phones is that they have different thermals and different power budgets from a console," says Lazarov. "They cannot just dissipate heat as much as a console can, as much as a PC can, and they are operating off of a battery all the time."

Web traffic rose 125% above average, causing the streaming platform to crash
Arm's solution to this involves integrating neural processing with the more traditional rendering pipe. "It can reduce the GPU workload and it can also reduce the power that the GPU consumes, which then also has knock-on effects on how efficient and capable your device is at the system level."
"So what that basically means is that you get this new efficiency, which helps remove some of the limitations that developers face. And it also helps them not have to worry about making trade-offs as much as they would normally do."
Neural Dawn: Showcasing the future of AI-powered mobile gaming
Watch on YouTube
To encourage developers to embrace the possibilities of AI-native graphics, Arm is adopting an open software approach, as well as providing a suite of tools. "We've been working really hard with the ecosystem over the past two years or so," says Lazarov. "The goal that we had was, let's find a way to use AI which is really developer friendly and allows developers to actually have access to these really big efficiency gains – they can then take that extra budget and then reinvest it in visual fidelity if they want to, performance if they want to, battery life if they want to, or a combination of those three things."
Related
Data: 96% of studios now run a direct-to-consumer web store or plan to
Survey published by FastSpring and Omdia finds 82% of devs say recent regulatory changes made them "more confident in the future value of D2C"
The key technologies include Neural Super Sampling (NSS), Neural Super Sampling and Denoising (NSSD), and Neural Frame Rate Upscaling (NFRU). Arm's technology is essentially able to upscale images and cast additional rays, as well as generate further frames using a form of AI reconstruction.
Lazarov gives an example of two frames. "In the first frame, what's happening is that the GPU is actually rendering just a quarter of the image, and then the remaining three quarters are being reconstructed on our neuro accelerators thanks to NSS," he says. "Then in the second frame, there's actually zero work happening in terms of traditional rendering on the GPU. All the pixels are coming thanks to the neuro accelerators, so everything is AI reconstructed."
Not like DLSS 5
Nvidia has also been working on AI-enabled technology with DLSS 5, which is able to add extra detail to images – but the technology has been met with controversy owing to the way it can potentially deviate from the developers' original intentions . Lazarov is at pains to point out that Arm's approach is nothing like Nvidia's.
DLSS 5 from Nvidia has been criticised for the way it can deviate from developers' intentions | Image credit: Nvidia/Capcom
"Our networks are not generative, so they're not from the same nature as the latest DLSS model," he says. "Our networks are convolution type networks, which means that they don't imagine anything, they don't create anything, they just kind of know what things need to look like. So we've trained our networks on real content, but we have also trained them in a way on data sets which allow us to actually make our networks open and public. So all of our networks, our resolution networks, our frame rate generation networks, all of those networks are public and open on GitHub and on Hugging Face.
"What this really means is that a developer can actually get one of our networks and then say, for example, if you have a game which is very quirky because you want to differentiate based on your art style, we give you all the tools that allow you to basically capture data sets from your quirky looking game and then retrain our network, so that our network knows exactly what your game looks like. And when it's upscaling the resolution and inserting new frames, it inserts them in exactly the way in which they should [look] like. And because you are the one who has done that retraining, there's no risk of loss of IP control or anything like that."
"DLSS is not open. It's not like our network. It's proprietary, it's closed, it's a black box, you don't know what's happening"
This approach is very different from the closed-box nature of DLSS 5, says Lazarov. "DLSS is not open. It's not like our network. It's proprietary, it's closed, it's a black box, you don't know what's happening, you don't know what it's trained on. You cannot retrain it on your own [data]. You integrate it, you're happy with the results, or you're not. It's a bit of a take it or leave it, whereas [ours] is take it and make it so that you like it."
Another big difference is that unlike DLSS 5, Arm's technology has been developed with a mobile-first approach, "meaning that our network is designed to operate within every single mobile constraint, be it power, bandwidth – all of those budgets are taken into account."
"If you take something like DLSS, it just wouldn't run on the phone, even if it had software support – you would blow past your budgets instantly."
Hyper-efficient
Lazarov emphasises how Arm has put a focus on reducing power usage with the Mali G2-Ultra NX. "In addition to these impressive results like 4X performance, 4X efficiency, we also have 70% reduction in the traffic out to DRAM, which is one of the biggest contributors to power consumption on a mobile," he says. "So the less you have to go out to external memory, the less power you burn."
To give an example of the advances of the new chip, he explains that even when pushing last year's GPU to its maximum limit, it could only run Neural Dawn at 40 fps – and only 15 fps under normal conditions. The new GPU, by contrast, can easily run the game at 60 fps.
"In the future we're going to be where the developers are, we're going to make it as easy as we can for them"
In terms of development tools for the new tech, Arm currently has plug-ins available for Unreal, and has a roadmap of expanding to other game engines. "Unity is definitely something that we're looking at, but for now we basically decided to prioritize Unreal." Of note, Arm recently announced a partnership with Unity China .
"In the future we're going to be where the developers are," says Lazarov. "We're going to make it as easy as we can for them. But we also know that many developers use custom game engines, and we cannot provide plug-ins for those custom game engines. But what we do have is an SDK, and the SDK just gives them a very streamlined pathway towards still having a very direct integration."
He adds that developers can take advantage of Arm's AI-native graphics on previous games. "If you take an existing title that is already shipping, and if you want to integrate our solutions into it, that can take you as little as three months to ship a new version that can have these things in it."
Lazarov notes that Neural Dawn was built by a team of fewer than 20 in less than 18 months, and that Arm's tech allows developers to "very quickly and easily make existing games look better, be more efficient, or whatever direction they like to go in – or we just allow them to ship these groundbreaking titles very quickly."

title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced debuts in Top 5 for PC and console revenue in July | Newzoo Charts
text:
Remakes and rereleases drove games revenue in July, with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced debuting in second on PC and fourth on console in Newzoo's charts.
The first remake in the Assassin's Creed franchise, Newzoo market analyst Mert Şahin noted that Black Flag Resynced's "performance demonstrates the commercial potential that can remain with established titles."
"Remakes can combine familiarity with meaningful updates, appealing to existing fans while making older experiences more accessible to new audiences."
Black Flag Resynced ranked at No.9 on Newzoo's Top 20 new games year-to-date by revenue, while Halo: Campaign Evolved was at No.20.
Ports of Call of Duty: Black Ops and Black Ops 2 were shadow-dropped on PlayStation 4 and 5, reaching sixth and first place, respectively, in the console revenue charts.
"While Black Flag Resynced shows the potential of substantially updating an established game, July's Call of Duty results demonstrate that straightforward ports can also generate significant commercial momentum," said Şahin.
"These examples highlight different approaches to managing a back catalogue. Substantial remakes can reposition older games for modern audiences, while straightforward re-releases can generate renewed demand with comparatively limited changes."
Elsewhere, Palworld left early access and entered the PC revenue chart in fifth place. Newzoo noted that, as a single-purchase title without microtransactions or paid DLC, most revenue came from new players.
Palworld 1.0 also debuted at No.19 on Newzoo's Top 20 new games year-to-date by revenue.
Looking at monthly active users (MAU) for console, Grand Theft Auto 5 rose two places, which Newzoo attributed to increased interest in GTA 6 following pre-orders and the launch of The Kortz Centre Heist on GTA Online.
"July's PC and console rankings show how publishers can create fresh momentum around established games and franchises," said Şahin.
"Timely in-game and real-world events lifted engagement, while remakes, re-releases, and lifecycle transitions generated new commercial opportunities across PC and console."
